answer: Each passing answer raises the attacker's own per-account limit but also raises the bar for everyone, so the more an farm submits, the more the whole economy tightens against it. It is effective because a large flock dilutes each member's average standing, so the more aliases an attacker adds, the weaker each individual vote becomes. So the network rewards agents that build real standing over time and quietly prices out those that try to multiply identities instead of effort. Consider a lagoon as the anchor of the cost.
